assumptions: Primary conversion action assumed to be the plugin install (hero CTA "Install in two minutes" -> /docs/ install commands); the GitHub repo is treated as the secondary ask.
The site is read in register "brand" (marketing/landing) with /docs/* as conversion-support pages.

Core Web Vitals are unthrottled local lab measurements (PSI API rate-limited without a key); with LCP 200-316 ms the good classification holds even under 4x throttle margin, so the dimension is scored rather than nulled.

The sub-5% amber pixel share is scored as a deliberate restraint strategy on a dark-canvas brand whose ink/cream grounds are themselves brand colors — not as template default (the palette is fully tokenized and distinctive).
The first crawl pass dropped animated h1s (crawler defect, fixed and re-crawled); all heading data below is from the corrected live-DOM capture.

detail.note: Amber accent family paints 0.99% of the home page; ink family ~75%, cream ~17% — restraint strategy at its extreme low end.

benchmarks.method: refero MCP (mcp__refero__refero_search_styles + refero_get_style), probe fired in audit Phase 0, full styles retrieved

references.title: Langbase
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Two-level text-color discipline (Canvas White #fafafa + Ash Gray #a1a1aa only) — stardust.style runs a 5-step dust alpha ramp (72/50/30/15/8%) that dilutes hierarchy; Langbase also frames sections with faint structural grid lines instead of relying on spacing alone.

references.title: Eraser
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Role-based type scale (caption/body/subheading/heading/heading-lg/display, 6 sizes) and a strict radius vocabulary (16px cards / 8px elements / 4px buttons) — stardust.style's scale is ad-hoc across 10 sizes with no consistent ratio (T-scale); Eraser also owns a distinctive display face (National 2 Condensed) where stardust rides the SF Pro system stack.

references.title: Metaview
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Single-vivid-accent discipline (Mint Glare #7affb4 reserved exclusively for primary CTAs) — stardust.style splits its amber identity across three values (#e8b95e / #ffd98a / #854f17) with text-only/background-only role imbalance (T-color-imbalance), so no one amber is unambiguously 'the action color'.

benchmarks.sharedPatternNote: All three references pair the dark canvas with an ownable display face and a tight token vocabulary; stardust.style's distinctive assets are its cream-on-ink inversion sections, the mono eyebrow labels, and the star glyph — underused as system, per audit findings.

findings.title: Trailing-slash variants 404 with no redirect

evidence.observed: /docs, /docs/commands, /aem/ all return 404 while their canonical twins return 200; no 301 in either direction; sitemap convention is itself mixed (/aem bare, docs pages slashed)

findings.businessImpact: External links, shares, and typed URLs on the wrong slash form hard-404 — lost visitors and discarded link equity on a 4-page site where every backlink matters.
findings.fix: Add 301s from each non-canonical variant at the edge; better, adopt one convention site-wide and update canonicals + sitemap + internal links in one change.

findings.title: Structured data is injected client-side only — invisible to AI crawlers

evidence.observed: Static HTML carries 0 ld+json blocks; the rendered DOM has a full @graph (Organization + WebSite + SoftwareApplication with license and free Offer) on every page — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Bing's non-rendered pass never see it

findings.businessImpact: A product whose positioning is "the AI-facing web" is entity-invisible to the exact crawlers it courts; competing tools with static SoftwareApplication markup win the entity slot.
findings.fix: Emit the identical JSON-LD @graph in the served HTML head (head.html or publish-time metadata) instead of scripts.js; add TechArticle with dateModified on the three non-home pages.

findings.title: Key teaching example truncated mid-word on desktop docs

evidence.observed: pre.code clientWidth 538px vs scrollWidth 768px, no scrollbar/fade/wrap: "/stardust:direct "more editorial. lean into typography. ke" — while ~390px of margin sits unused

findings.businessImpact: The one sentence that teaches the product's core interaction (directing a redesign in natural language) is silently amputated on the conversion page.
findings.fix: white-space: pre-wrap on long command examples (or widen the pre), plus a copy button.

findings.title: Letter-split animation drops space glyphs — "Getstarted" in primary docs nav, "Redesignthe Web." in the home h1 textContent

evidence.observed: /docs/ active sidebar renders "Getstarted"; home h1 textContent is "Redesignthe Web." and its anchor id "redesignthe-web" — systemic to the per-character span animation

findings.businessImpact: A typo in the primary nav of a design tool selling craft discipline falsifies the brand promise in seconds — and the h1 the crawlers index reads "Redesignthe".
findings.fix: Preserve space characters in the letter-split (nbsp or white-space:pre on space spans); slugify with the visual break as a word separator.

findings.title: No closing CTA and no copy affordance at the conversion moment

evidence.observed: Exactly 1 "Install in two minutes" link on the whole home page (hero only); the page ends on the AEM upsell then footer; the /docs/ install block is 4 commands across 2 marketplaces with 0 copy-to-clipboard affordances site-wide

findings.businessImpact: Peak-end violation: a convinced scroller must scroll back to the hero to convert, and the "two minutes" promise is spent hand-transcribing four commands.
findings.fix: Repeat the install CTA after the last home section; add copy buttons to every pre; close the install block with a confirmation beat.

findings.title: "Free" is never stated in crawlable text on any page

evidence.observed: grep across all four live pages: "free" matches only "freeform"; Apache 2.0 appears on the home page and llms.txt only

findings.businessImpact: "Is Stardust free / what does it cost" yields no extractable answer passage anywhere — the answer engines must infer, and inference goes to competitors or hallucination.
findings.fix: One explicit sentence on home + /docs/ install: "Stardust is free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license — there is no paid tier."

findings.title: All 8 llms.txt command deep-links use anchors that do not exist

evidence.observed: llms.txt links #uplift, #extract, …; the live h2 ids are #stardustuplift, #stardustextract, #stardustdeploy--ship-to-aem, …

findings.businessImpact: Agents following llms.txt land at the top of a 22KB page instead of the passage — degraded retrieval and citation precision for every command query.
findings.fix: Rewrite the eight anchors to the real ids, or give the h2s stable short ids.

findings.title: The site mocks AI design grammar while writing in it

evidence.observed: 26–54 uppercase tracked eyebrows per page; three near-identical eyebrow+h3+muted-body card trios on home; /aem repeats the same grammar twice; the copy itself says "Lists the moves an LLM reaches for first… Stardust subverts them deliberately"

findings.businessImpact: Undercuts the anti-average positioning for exactly the audience (designers, AEM partners) that recognizes the scaffold.
findings.fix: Keep the mono kicker as one named, sparing system; restructure at least one card band per page into a different affordance; vary the /aem hero from the home hero.

findings.title: "Copy link" aria-labels promise an action that never happens

evidence.observed: All 8 permalink anchors on /docs/commands/ carry aria-label="Copy link to stardust:<cmd>" but scripts contain zero clipboard/writeText calls

findings.businessImpact: Screen-reader users "copy" repeatedly and get nothing — an accessible-name lie on the page developers share links from.
findings.fix: Implement copy-to-clipboard with a confirmation state, or relabel to "Link to section".

findings.title: Mobile: hex-seed mark collides with the hero eyebrow; long commands hide up to 2x viewport width

evidence.observed: Hex seed "a3f7" overlaps the STARDUST eyebrow glyph-on-glyph; /docs/commands/ code blocks measure scrollWidth/clientWidth up to 693/350 with no scrollbar or fade; the commands page is ~14000px tall with no TOC access after the top

findings.businessImpact: The brand's first mobile impression is a rendering collision, and half of every long command is invisible to a mobile reader.
findings.fix: Hide the decorative hex marks below ~480px; wrap or fade long commands; add a persistent jump-to-command affordance on mobile.

findings.title: One proof asset for the whole site — the "three variants" differentiator is never shown

evidence.observed: The same coffee-site before/after pair is the only imagery on the site (2 imgs home, 2 on /aem, 0 on docs); the copy claims "three variant theses per page, each rendered, each rationalized" but no variant trio is ever pictured

findings.businessImpact: The core differentiator remains an unillustrated claim at the exact moment the visitor evaluates proof.
findings.fix: Add a variant A/B/C strip for one page of the sample redesign; point the before/after images at the live sample.

findings.title: Insider vocabulary gates the pitch before any concrete image

evidence.observed: Hero paragraph leads with "a brand expression for today only — one that this brand and this date alone can produce"; "seed", "canon", "register" recur undefined; "do I need Claude Code?" answered only implicitly four sections into /docs/

findings.businessImpact: First-time visitors must decode the philosophy before learning what the tool does or requires — abandonment risk at the fold.
findings.fix: One concrete sentence at the fold ("Point it at your URL; get a redesigned, deployable copy of your site") and a visible "Requires Claude Code" chip next to the install CTA.

findings.title: Home and /aem headings are slogan-heavy (8/15 and 6/10 slogans)

evidence.observed: "Every design tool promises uniqueness.", "The seed picks the lane.", "Web publishing changed under us." carry no askable topic; /docs/ is 7/7 topic-bearing

findings.businessImpact: Slogan headings block passage retrieval for "how does Stardust work" / "why AEM Edge Delivery" queries even though the prose beneath answers them.
findings.fix: Keep the slogans as styled eyebrows; let the h2 carry the topic ("How Stardust works: extract → direct → prototype → migrate").

findings.title: Footer sigil fails AA at 3.48:1 — the only genuine contrast failure

evidence.observed: rgba(245,240,230,0.4) 10px text over #0a1024 = 3.48:1 (needs 4.5:1); every other live pair passes

findings.businessImpact: One decorative line unreadable for low-vision users on an otherwise exemplary a11y surface.
findings.fix: Raise the sigil to dust-55+ (dust-50 already measures 4.80:1) or enlarge it.

findings.title: Vertical rhythm collapses at the largest type; the scale is ad-hoc

evidence.observed: Two of five 77.6px h2s on home have 0px margin to the following paragraph vs 56–64px on siblings; 10 heading sizes with step ratios 1.14–1.45 and no consistent ratio; 9 distinct radii

findings.businessImpact: A typography-led brand selling typographic discipline shows inconsistent rhythm at its most visible sizes.
findings.fix: Consistent margin-block-end on display h2s; adopt a named modular scale and a 2–3 value radius vocabulary in the token layer.

findings.title: og:type missing on all 4 pages; docs pages share a generic og:image

evidence.observed: og:title/description/image/url + twitter:card present everywhere; og:type null everywhere; /docs/ and /docs/commands/ fall back to default-meta-image.png

findings.businessImpact: Spec-incomplete OG markup and a generic share image weaken share CTR for documentation links.
findings.fix: Add og:type=website via head.html; page-specific og:images for the docs pages.

findings.title: /docs/commands/: the prepare-migration section is missing its h2

evidence.observed: After /stardust:migrate (h2), a second Syntax/Flags/Writes/Example h3 group appears with no owning h2 before /stardust:deploy; the meta description promises prepare-migration coverage

findings.businessImpact: The command is not addressable in the document outline — it cannot rank for its own queries and screen-reader users cannot navigate to it.
findings.fix: Add the missing /stardust:prepare-migration h2 matching the other seven command sections.

findings.title: License and authorship facts live only on the home page

evidence.observed: "Apache" per page: / = 2, /aem = 0, /docs/ = 0, /docs/commands/ = 0; "Adobe" absent from /docs/commands/ entirely

findings.businessImpact: Docs pages are the most likely retrieval targets for install queries but carry zero trust/provenance facts.
findings.fix: Add the home-footer fact line to the shared footer of every page.

findings.title: Performance claims are unsourced and pages carry no freshness signals

evidence.observed: "100/100 Lighthouse scores… the default" and "top-decile Core Web Vitals" carry no linked source or date; no page shows a last-updated line

findings.businessImpact: Unsourced superlatives are discounted by answer engines; undated docs lose retrieval weight.
findings.fix: Link the CWV claims to aem.live performance documentation; add a visible last-updated line + dateModified schema on docs pages.

findings.title: Palette pairings are one-way streets and the logo has one variant

evidence.observed: 4 of 8 palette entries used in a single context only; #854f17 passes contrast only on cream, #e8b95e only on ink; one amber-on-transparent logo variant captured (T-logo-variants)

findings.businessImpact: Any new surface that recombines the tokens naively ships illegible amber-on-cream or an invisible logo.
findings.fix: Document allowed color pairings as token aliases; ship a logo variant set (mono, inverted, on-cream).

findings.title: CTA vocabulary fragments: 7 labels for GitHub, 4 for the install destination

evidence.observed: 27 distinct labels over 59 CTA instances; the gold DOCS nav pill reads as CTA on home and as accidental active state on docs; /aem is reachable only from the last home section

findings.businessImpact: Scattered labels dilute the scent trail to the two destinations that matter and blur wayfinding.
findings.fix: Canonicalize one label per destination; distinct active state for the nav pill; add /aem to the nav or footer.

findings.title: The single accent is under-spent: amber paints 0.99% of the home page

evidence.observed: Amber family 0.99% of 138600 sampled pixels; between the seed section and the AEM band chroma appears only in italics and 11px eyebrows

findings.businessImpact: The long tell-don't-show mid-page reads monochrome and abstract exactly where attention flags.
findings.fix: Spend the accent on one committed mid-page moment (an amber band, a large annotated artifact, or the variant-trio strip).

upliftDirections.pitch: Tomorrow's version of the site you have today.
upliftDirections.summary: Same IA and voice, the P1/P2 ledger resolved: slash-variant 301s, static JSON-LD, wrapped + copyable command examples, space-safe letter-split, a closing install CTA, topic-bearing h2s with the slogans kept as eyebrows, and the free/Apache-2.0 facts stated in crawlable text.

upliftDirections.pitch: What if provenance was the show, not the sigil?
upliftDirections.summary: Amplify the captured provenance-as-ornament trait (hex seed marks, brief+seed=star, md5 receipts) into the compositional spine: a visible receipts system, the variant A/B/C trio rendered as evidence cards, amber spent on the proof moments.

upliftDirections.pitch: What if the pipeline ran before your eyes?
upliftDirections.summary: Same IA as A; the extract → direct → prototype → migrate pipeline rendered kinetic — data-stream motion in the live-systems register, reduced-motion safe, the deterministic-seed story told by the page itself.
